stem: The histogram summarizes a data set of 50 values. Each interval includes its left endpoint but not its right endpoint. Which of the following could be the mean of the data set?
solution: The mean is smallest if every value is at the left endpoint of its interval: \(\frac{10(5) + 20(12) + 30(18) + 40(10) + 50(5)}{50} = \frac{1{,}480}{50} = 29.6\).
The mean is largest if every value is just below the right endpoint of its interval, which gives a mean just below \(29.6 + 10 = 39.6\).
So the mean must be at least 29.6 and less than 39.6. Of the choices, only 34 is in this range.

explanation.A: Correct. The mean must be between 29.6 and 39.6, and 34 is the only choice in that range.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Even if every value were at the left endpoint of its interval, the mean would be 29.6, so the mean cannot be 28.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Even if every value were at the top of its interval, the mean would be less than 39.6, so the mean cannot be 41.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the number of values in the data set, not a possible mean.

verify:
bins = figure['bins']
n = sum(f for lo, hi, f in bins)
assert n == 50
low = Rational(sum(lo * f for lo, hi, f in bins), n)
high = Rational(sum(hi * f for lo, hi, f in bins), n)
assert low == Rational('29.6') and high == Rational('39.6')
ok = [k for k in choices if low <= value(choices[k]) < high]
assert ok == [answer] and value(choices[answer]) == 34
